title: Preadditive and Additive Categories and Biproducts

items.title: Preadditive category
A one-object preadditive category is the same thing as a ring
items.strategy: Identify the unique hom-group with the ring's additive group, take composition as multiplication, and use functoriality plus additivity to recover exactly the unital ring-homomorphism laws.

items.title: Additive functors from a ring to abelian groups are left modules
items.strategy: Unpack an additive functor on the one-object category attached to a ring as an action by endomorphisms, and read naturality of a transformation as module-linearity.

items.title: Additive functor
An additive functor preserves zero morphisms
items.strategy: An additive functor carries the zero element of each hom-group to the zero element of the target hom-group.

items.title: The opposite of a preadditive category is preadditive
items.strategy: The opposite category has the same hom-groups, and reversing composition preserves bilinearity because the original composition is bilinear in both variables.

items.title: A small product of preadditive categories is preadditive
items.strategy: Use componentwise abelian-group operations on each hom-set and check bilinearity coordinatewise.

items.title: Additive functors and natural transformations form a preadditive category
items.strategy: Add natural transformations pointwise, use the codomain hom-group laws objectwise, and cite the small-source size theorem to keep the hom-collections sets.

items.title: In a preadditive category, an object is initial exactly when it is terminal
items.strategy: Either universal property makes the endomorphism group trivial, so the identity equals zero and every map to or from the object is forced to be the unique zero arrow.

items.title: In a preadditive category with a zero object, the zero morphism is the neutral element of each hom-group
items.strategy: Compare the published zero morphism A -> 0 -> B with the additive identity by composing with arbitrary arrows and using uniqueness through the zero object.

items.title: A preadditive category with a zero object has zero morphisms in the published sense
items.strategy: Combine the published zero-object construction with the identification of those arrows with the hom-group zero elements.

items.title: Canonical morphism from a finite coproduct to a finite product
Biproduct
Biproduct data characterisation without addition
items.strategy: From a biproduct, read off the product and coproduct cones and the four zero equations; conversely, the same equations plus the universal properties identify one object as both.

items.title: The empty biproduct is a zero object
items.strategy: The empty coproduct is initial and the empty product is terminal, so an isomorphism between them makes the same object both.

items.title: Biproducts are associative, commutative, and unital up to canonical isomorphism
items.strategy: Transport the standard product and coproduct uniqueness isomorphisms across the canonical comparison that identifies each product with the corresponding coproduct.

items.title: A category with finite biproducts is enriched in commutative monoids
items.strategy: Define f + g using the diagonal into A + A and codiagonal out of B + B, then verify commutativity, associativity, zero, and bilinearity from the biproduct identities.

items.title: The commutative-monoid enrichment of a category with finite biproducts is unique
items.strategy: Any bilinear commutative-monoid law compatible with the same biproduct structure must reproduce the diagonal-codiagonal formula that defines addition.

items.title: The uniqueness of the enrichment is an Eckmann-Hilton phenomenon
items.strategy: Apply Eckmann-Hilton to two candidate bilinear monoid laws with the same unit and interchange supplied by composition.

items.title: Semiadditive category
On a biproduct, the injections and projections satisfy the identity-sum relation
items.strategy: Expand the diagonal-codiagonal formula on A + B to show i_A p_A + i_B p_B = 1, and use the same equality together with the zero equations to recover the universal properties.

items.title: A semiadditive category is preadditive exactly when every morphism has an additive inverse
items.strategy: The semiadditive hom-sets are already commutative monoids with bilinear composition, so preadditivity is exactly the extra existence of negatives.

items.title: Additive category
In a preadditive category, a finite product is automatically a biproduct
items.strategy: Use zero morphisms to define the coproduct injections from a product cone, and use the nullary case to identify the terminal object with an initial one.

items.title: Additive categories are closed under passage to the opposite
items.strategy: The opposite stays preadditive, and finite products in the opposite are finite coproducts in the original, hence again biproducts.

items.title: Morphisms between finite biproducts correspond to matrices
items.strategy: Recover a map from its projection-component-injection entries by summing injection-component-projection composites, and prove bijectivity by decomposing the identities of the source and target biproducts.

items.title: Composition between finite biproducts is matrix multiplication
items.strategy: Insert the identity decomposition of the middle biproduct and read off the resulting entrywise sum using the matrix representation theorem.

items.title: The biproduct of morphisms is the diagonal matrix
items.strategy: Apply the matrix-entry formula to the block map obtained by taking a biproduct of the given morphisms.

items.title: An infinite coproduct need not agree with the infinite product
items.strategy: In Ab, compare the finite-support subgroup direct sum_n Z with the full product of all sequences and use the constant 1-sequence as a non-image of the canonical map.

items.title: The additive category of matrices over a ring
The matrix category over a ring is additive
items.strategy: Use block injections and projections to exhibit m + n as the biproduct of m and n, with matrix addition on hom-sets inherited entrywise from the ring.

items.title: The matrix category is equivalent to the finitely generated free modules
items.strategy: Send n to R^n and a matrix to the corresponding linear map on column vectors; full faithfulness is matrix arithmetic and the essential image is exactly the finitely generated free modules.

items.title: The matrix category is the finite-biproduct completion of a ring
In a preadditive category, the equalizer of a parallel pair is the kernel of their difference
items.strategy: Equalizing f and g is equivalent to forcing their difference f - g to vanish, so the universal properties coincide.

items.title: In a preadditive category, the coequalizer of a parallel pair is the cokernel of their difference
items.strategy: Pass to the opposite category and apply the equalizer-as-kernel theorem there.

items.title: An additive category with all kernels and cokernels has all finite limits and colimits
items.strategy: Finite limits reduce to products and equalizers, with products coming from preadditivity and equalizers from kernels; dualize for colimits.

items.title: In a preadditive category with a zero object, a morphism is monic exactly when its kernel is zero
items.strategy: If a kernel is zero, any equality fu = fv gives f(u - v) = 0 and forces u - v to factor through zero; conversely, a monic map makes its kernel arrow factor through the zero object.

items.title: In a preadditive category with a zero object, a morphism is epic exactly when its cokernel is zero
items.strategy: Apply the monic-kernel criterion in the opposite preadditive category.

items.title: A zero kernel does not force monicity in a merely semiadditive category
items.strategy: In CMon, the quotient q: N -> {0,a} with a+a=a has trivial kernel but identifies the maps sending 1 to 1 and 1 to 2, so q is not monic.

items.title: An additive functor preserves finite biproducts
items.strategy: Apply the functor to the biproduct equations and use additivity plus preservation of zero morphisms to keep the identities and zero entries intact.

items.title: A functor between additive categories is additive exactly when it preserves finite biproducts
items.strategy: One direction is biproduct preservation by additivity; conversely, recover F(f + g) from preservation of the diagonal, codiagonal, and the binary biproducts.

items.title: A functor between additive categories preserving finite products is additive
items.strategy: Finite products are finite biproducts in an additive category, so the biproduct criterion applies.

items.title: Any adjoint between additive categories is additive
items.strategy: Right adjoints preserve finite limits and left adjoints preserve finite colimits; in an additive category either side is enough to recover biproduct preservation.

items.title: An additive functor is left exact exactly when it preserves kernels
items.strategy: Finite limits are products plus equalizers; additive functors preserve finite products, and equalizers are kernels of differences in a preadditive setting.

items.title: An additive functor preserves split biproduct diagrams
items.strategy: Apply the functor to the chosen injection, projection, section, and retraction maps and reuse the preserved biproduct identities.

items.title: The Hom bifunctor of a preadditive category takes values in abelian groups
items.strategy: Each hom-set already carries an abelian-group structure, and pre- and post-composition are homomorphisms by biadditivity.

items.title: Hom functors on a preadditive category are left exact
items.strategy: View Hom(A,-) as covariantly representable and Hom(-,B) as representable on the opposite category, then invoke the published theorem that representables preserve limits.

items.title: The published module statement is the instance of this corollary
A covariant hom functor on an additive category need not preserve cokernels
items.strategy: Apply Hom(Z/2,-) to Z --2--> Z -> Z/2 and compute that the induced map on hom-groups is not surjective onto the cokernel.

items.title: Idempotent and split idempotent
A splitting of an idempotent is simultaneously an equalizer and a coequalizer and is unique up to unique isomorphism
items.strategy: Use the relations ip = e and pi = 1 to show i equalizes e and 1 while p coequalizes them, then identify any two splittings by the corresponding universal properties.

items.title: Idempotent-complete category
An additive category with kernels is idempotent complete
items.strategy: For an idempotent e, take the kernel of 1 - e and use the additive splitting identities to show that this kernel object is exactly the image summand of e.

items.title: The idempotent completion of a preadditive category
The idempotent completion is idempotent complete, and its inclusion is fully faithful and universal
items.strategy: Build Kar(C) explicitly from pairs (A,e), prove split idempotents inside it, show the inclusion A -> (A,1_A) is fully faithful, and extend functors by sending (A,e) to a chosen splitting image of F(e).

items.title: The addition on an additive category is extra structure that must be chosen
items.strategy: Refute the claim by citing the uniqueness theorem showing that the biproduct structure forces a single possible addition law on every hom-set.

items.title: A category with finite products and finite coproducts has biproducts
items.strategy: Refute the claim in pointed sets, where the zero object and both finite constructions exist but the canonical map from wedge to product need not be an isomorphism.

items.title: A functor preserving zero morphisms is additive
items.strategy: Use the reduced free-abelian-group functor on underlying pointed sets: it preserves zero morphisms but does not preserve sums of homomorphisms.

items.title: A preadditive category with a zero object has binary biproducts
items.strategy: Refute the claim with the full subcategory of Ab on 0 and Z, where hom-groups and a zero object exist but Z x Z is not an object.

items.title: Every idempotent splits
items.strategy: Refute the claim by exhibiting a preadditive category whose formal idempotent completion strictly enlarges it, so some idempotent is unsplit before completion.

title: Preadditive and Additive Categories and Biproducts - Examples

items.title: The biproduct of two abelian groups computed as a matrix calculus
items.strategy: Write the injections, projections, diagonal, and codiagonal in Ab and compute a sample composite entrywise as an ordinary matrix product.

items.title: Abelian groups, modules, and vector spaces are additive
items.strategy: Use the familiar pointwise hom-group structures and products, then invoke the additive-category criterion to package the standard examples together.

items.title: A ring viewed as a one-object preadditive category with its matrices
items.strategy: Start from the single-object ring category and then display its finite-biproduct completion as block matrices of all finite sizes.

items.title: The idempotent completion of a ring is the finitely generated projective modules
items.strategy: Identify an object (R^n,e) with the retract of the free module R^n cut out by the idempotent matrix e, and recognize those retracts as the finitely generated projectives.

items.title: Pointed sets are not additive
items.strategy: Compute the wedge and product of two nontrivial pointed sets and show that the canonical map from the wedge to the product is not an isomorphism.

items.title: Commutative monoids are semiadditive and not additive
items.strategy: Use the standard finite product-coproduct coincidence in CMon, then note that additive inverses fail and the zero-kernel witness already records the obstruction.

items.title: Additive functors out of the matrix category
items.strategy: Translate an additive functor out of Mat_R through the finite-free-module equivalence and read it as a finite-biproduct-preserving module construction.

items.title: A preadditive category with two objects and a nonzero hom-group
items.strategy: Specify two objects, choose abelian groups for all four hom-sets, and define a bilinear composition law directly.
